title: Standing Firm in Faith
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child names Antioch as where believers were first called Christians (Acts 11:26), retells how Stephen was stoned and prayed for his killers (Acts 7:54-60), lists lessons, and explains why not to join groups that mock God.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the church began at Pentecost.
floor.question: Where did the church begin?

representations: a map with Jerusalem and Antioch
steps: Stephen speaks boldly and the leaders are furious.
He sees Jesus at God's right hand.
They stone him; Saul holds the coats.
He prays "do not hold this sin against them".
contexts: a group at school that mocks church
a Christian standing firm in hard times

board.do: Write Acts 7:60: "Lord, do not hold this sin against them".

board.say: What does Stephen's prayer teach us?

board.do: Wait for the child to say forgive, stand firm.
List three lessons on the board.

misconceptions.ask: What did Stephen pray for those stoning him?
In which city were believers first called Christians?
misconceptions.repair: Find Antioch on a Bible map.

misconceptions.ask: Your friends join a group that mocks Jesus. What should you do?
Who looked after the coats of the men who stoned Stephen (Acts 7:58)?
misconceptions.repair: Read Acts 7:58 and say: this Saul later became the apostle Paul.

checks.question: Where were believers first called Christians?
What did Stephen pray for those stoning him?
checks.answer: That God would not hold this sin against them
